        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
It assumes you have `git`, `docker`, `kubectl` and `gh` (GitHub CLI) installed and that you have the necessary permissions to push to the repository.

> **⚠️ Important** – The commands below will actually modify the repository.  
> Make sure you have a clean working tree (no uncommitted changes) before running them.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create the required files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a `Dockerfile` at the root of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – lightweight Node.js runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why node:18‑alpine?*  
> It’s small, secure, and contains the latest LTS Node.js release.  
> Adjust the port (`EXPOSE 3000`) if your app uses a different one.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can keep it under a `k8s/` folder for clarity):

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use Docker Hub
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> *What this does:*  
> * Deployment – 2 replicas of the container.  
> * Service – Exposes the pods on port 80 inside the cluster (you can change `type` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you want external access).

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a workflow file at `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build the Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest \
            --tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            .

      # Push the image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}
```

> **Secrets required**  
> * `GITHUB_TOKEN` – automatically available in GitHub Actions.  
> * If you prefer Docker Hub, replace the login step with `docker/login-action@v3` using `username` and `password` secrets.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
# Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
# Commit the changes
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to the main branch
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the Docker image, and push it to GitHub Container Registry.

---

## 5️⃣ (Optional) Deploy to a cluster

If you have a Kubernetes cluster configured with `kubectl`, you can apply the manifests:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

---

### Recap of the files added

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes Docker image |

Feel free to tweak the image tags, registry, or Kubernetes settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
